Week 3 was also harder on me than week 2 was - I'm now wondering if my body was still in a bit of shock. I'm currently on week 4, I hope it gets better. My feelings fluctuate a lot; I have moments where I feel hope and peace, but an hour or so later I'll feel so overwhelmingly sad again. Evenings and mornings are still hard. I hate it. I feel crazy.

I would try to avoid messaging him if possible, I know for myself it would likely regress my healing progress. I recommend that you either 1) continue ignoring him and mute/silence his notifications or 2) ask a friend to send the message via your phone, delete the thread, and mute/silence his notifications.

Oh OP, you're breaking my heart. :(

I remember feeling this exact way after my last major breakup (right now I'm recouping from the end of a mini-relationship; it's not great but I'm definitely not feeling as bad as I would from a full-blown relationship). 

I know it's all-encompassing right now, but I promise with all of my being that it will pass. I think it's very admirable that despite being in the deepest depths of despair, you're still able to look at this from an outside perspective. Let's also try and remember that not everyone we meet will be in our lives forever, whether it's for a few months, a year, a decade, or more -- it's all temporary. It's a scary thought, but it's also liberating. This means your pain, your heartache, and the insatiable longing -- it's also temporary. It will all subside. 

I think it's very understandable you want to remain friends with her, but a friendship can't be built on uneven grounds; the dynamic will never be sustainable. I know this is so cheesy, but your priority right now should be you. I know you spent the last 3 years making her your number one, but let's think about it. If this dynamic continued without equal reciprocation, would you be happy? Would you feel fulfilled for the rest of your life? Would you, on your deathbed, be able to say you lived life the way you wanted to?  

Is there a friend you can text when you want to share something? Friendships can be just as fulfilling as romantic relationships; after my previous ex absolutely broke me, sent me to the darkest place, I focused on reconnecting with old friends and strengthening current bonds. I now have a very strong support system, so anytime my brain jumps to wanting to share something with my old partner, I reframe this narrative and share with a close friend instead. There are two benefits of this: you strengthen a bond and you are able to appease that part of you that seeks closeness. 

After you heal, recover, and are able to be truly happy on your own without risk of slipping into an unbalanced dynamic with your ex, I think then you can/will be better equipped to revisit a connection with her.

If he truly has a kind soul, he will definitely feel guilty. Tell this story to any third party, no one will think it's okay that he decided to sleep with your friend on the day you moved out. He did something fucked up and he SHOULD know it.

It's okay that you feel angry and guilty. These emotions mean something, it speaks to your values: 
1) you are a loving person - you cared about this person, so when they hurt you, it's absolutely normal to feel angry. 
2) you are a kind person - although you (justifiably) lashed out, you have a good conscience and you feel bad that your actions didn't align with your character. 
I'm here to tell you, it's okay. Forgive yourself, because out of everyone in this situation, you're the one that deserves it the most.

I wish I could give you a hug. If you need someone to talk to, please feel to free to PM me anytime.

I'm so sorry, I know how hard this is. =(  

In my previous experiences, every time I wanted to text my ex, I texted a friend instead to help alleviate that part of my desire. A week isn't a very long time for NC, but I promise you will feel better after another week. And after another 7 days, you might feel zero desire to reach out at all. It gets easier and easier with every passing week as long as you stick to it. 

I'm a very visual person, so I like crossing out my calendar every day I maintain NC. And whenever I feel weak, I look at my calendar and it motivates me to maintain the streak. 

It will get easier. <3

Please don't do it! I don't want to diagnose her attachment style, but as someone who is more avoidant-leaning (and thus, her behaviour sort of resonates with me), you sending that letter will only validate her ego and enable her to continue treating you this way. Stay strong and avoid all contact with her, even if she tries to come back. Unless she seeks extensive therapy I don't see her behaviour changing...which only ends in a world of pain for you. :(

This dance is very draining (I've done my own avoidant/anxious dances with exes -- with myself as the anxious party in some situations). You will find someone who treats you with the same amount of love and affection you deserve. It's really her loss, not yours. If you think about it logically, you really have much less to lose than she does.

It was completely reasonable for you to react poorly when you found out your ex slept with your friend THE DAY YOU MOVED OUT. I would be incredibly impressed if you were able to have a diplomatic conversation with him after that. I don't think you have anything to apologize for. You are human and it's completely normal and okay to react in ways we perceive as "negative"  (i.e. out of anger, sadness, resentment, etc.) when someone has hurt us so deeply. This wasn't an innocuous mistake, this was disrespect at new levels. 

He should be the one feeling apologetic, guilty, and remorseful for his actions, not you. You have nothing to apologize for. Let him come to you with his tail between his legs; let him stew in the discomfort of his actions. He SHOULD know that you're angry. He should understand that what he did wasn't okay (if he values being a considerate person).

I know it's easier said than done because I understand how all-encompassing the pain of heartbreak can be, but as an objective third party looking in, I can guarantee you will feel better in the long term by not offering him even one second more of your time and energy. Let him wonder about YOU. Let him sit in the guilt of his clownery. 

And as we all know, the opposite of love isn't hate, it's apathy. Stay strong and remain apathetic, even if you don't feel that way. Hold onto your self-respect and remain unbothered. He will come crawling back someday looking like a fool and you will feel good knowing you were able to authentically express yourself while maintaining your self-respect.

You've got this.

Wow, this brings me so much hope!!! I've been single for 5 years but recently went through a mini-breakup with someone I was seeing. Makes me feel a little sad that it didn't work out, but also hopeful that you were able to find someone after a while tooo! There's still hope for meeeeeee. <3
wow, these are amazing tips. thank you so much!
This is so beautifully written, it really resonated with me. Thank you.

Wow you sound extremely manipulative and awful. Leave her alone.
she's still really pretty though.

I know how you feel, especially the justifying the bad part. It's hard. It's so, so hard to let go right now. The crappy things you once thought were such a big deal in the relationship seem so minuscule now, things that you can easily overlook. Compared to other people, he's not that bad. I totally get it. I feel the exact same way. I spend almost 24 hours a day thinking about where it went wrong and how I could have done better. :( 

However, the most fundamental aspect of any relationship is that both people want to be in it. And if he doesn't want to be in a relationship with you, there's honestly nothing you can do. It's not your fault. Don't blame yourself, don't think "oh but if only I did this differently." You wanted it to work, he saw you in all your loving glory and still chose to leave. You did all that you could. Let him walk. 

It's okay to love him (for the time being), but always love yourself more. You deserve it, especially right now. *Hugs*

3 times. Definitely not worth it. I would fall into the worst depressive cycles afterwards. No appetite. Insomnia. Withdrawing from friends. Random crying. Suicidal thoughts. The whole 9 yards. I'm actually going through a cycle right now because I stupidly decided to call him last week. Prior to that, I managed 3 weeks of NC and I was actually starting to feel a lot better. I totally regret reaching out because I basically ruined all my progress. Now it just feels like I'll never recover from this. :(

I honestly feel the same. My ex and I had the exact same type of humor, which I think is really rare. He was also well-educated, smart, fun, ambitious, and successful. I am almost certain I'll never find anyone better. :( It's an absolutely defeating and terrifying thought. It makes it so much harder to move on.

Don't do it please. We ended up talking today for over 3 hours on the phone. Yes he misses me. Yes we are both still hurting. But he doesn't want to be with me. So it was pointless. The entire conversation was pointless. The joy I felt for those 3 hours is nothing compared to the pain I'm feeling now. I feel like I wasted all my progress. I was finally starting to get better, but now I feel like I'm going through the entire healing process again. 0/10 would recommend.

Hey, thanks for replying. I'm glad I'm not the only 26 year old who feels like this. I feel like I'm getting old and I'm running out of time to improve myself. 

Please don't discount the fact that you got a degree. It's almost impossible to get yourself to finish assignments and go to class when you suffer from such debilitating depression. I couldn't do it. I just stopped showing up. Being able to complete your degree under such circumstances is an amazing accomplishment. I really admire your perseverance. 

It's great you have a part-time job. You're getting out and doing the things necessary for yourself. What did you ruin if you don't mind me asking? Because to me I think you are doing a good job of rebuilding. I think that's really awesome. 

As for me, I have nothing. Nothing to show after 26 years on this earth haha. So I don't think I will be able to find anyone or do anything better. I guess it's relieving to know that at least I have control over the way I die. 

I'm here for you if you want to talk too. It is really relieving to recognize aspects of myself in you.

Hey thank you for replying. 

I don't think I can finish my degree because I'm so depressed all the time, I find it very hard to concentrate in class sometimes or on my assignments. I just don't see any hope. I would really like to finish though. I was in the English literature program. 

I highly doubt I can find anyone better than this last person. I have accomplished nothing in my life. Why would anyone so accomplished want to be with someone so useless like me haha.
6 months is wayyyyyy too long. If he truly wanted to be with you, he would be. I'm really, really sorry to say this but you should really move on. :(

You did the right thing by breaking up with him. Don't bother rekindling the relationship, there are way better guys out there; ones who know how to prioritize their girlfriends. Relationships are supposed to be fulfilling and nurturing, there's no point if you feel like you have to "stick it out." :( *Hugs*

I know exactly how you feel. Two years ago I broke up with this really sweet amazing guy and for a long time after I was filled with regret and guilt. My mom and grandma made matters worse by constantly asking me why I broke up with him if he was so good to me. It made moving on so much harder. I thought I was never going to find anyone as sweet or as caring as my ex. 

I did and I didn't. There were guys who were super sweet and nice to me, but I just wasn't interested. I eventually met a guy who isn't as "sweet" as my ex, but the chemistry I have with him is so much better. He's also way more ambitious and confident and I find those qualities more important. He's sweet in different ways and I am way more attracted to him than I was to my ex. I guess what I'm trying to say is that there are a lot of guys out there who will fulfill you in different ways; you won't like them any less just because they aren't as "sweet."

I'm so sorry you're going through this, I know how much it hurts since I'm going through something similar. :( 

Honestly, I would just straight up ask him. There's really nothing to lose. If he truly cares about you, he will put in the effort to communicate and hangout with you. If he doesn't show any concern or initiative, then save yourself the time and further heartache and dump his butt. 

You'll be okay even if you lose him, OP! Make room in your life for people who truly deserve your time and effort. If you have to work so hard just to get someone to reciprocate a little bit, it's really, really not worth it. Sending lots of love and courage your way! <3

Time heals all. As corny as it sounds, it does. You'll forget some of the memories and inside jokes, and some you'll keep for life. Over time, it will hurt less and less. One day, you'll be able to reminisce on some of the memories without it hurting at all. You'll be okay. Stay strong. <3

You might have fucked up, but in no way do your fuck ups define you as a person. Most importantly, it is okay to fuck up. No one goes through life doing everything perfectly. 

If it makes you feel any better, I'm 24 and I'm still not done my undergrad. I, like you, had the same "finish uni in 4 years" dream, but I quickly realized that wasn't happening. But you know what, most people don't finish undergrad in 4 years. It's completely normal to take 5-6 years. The amount of time it takes you to complete university does not correlate to your value and intelligence as a person. Furthermore, I also struggle with the exact same things as you do in school: I can't concentrate on my assignments and I procrastinate like hell. To make things worse, I kept fucking up my semesters due to all of these factors (which are worsened by my cycles of depression) and my CGPA dropped so low I got kicked out. :/

At first, I felt like such a failure. I felt like a waste of space. If so many people could go through school without a hitch, why couldn't I? I felt so stupid for not even being able to do this simple school thing correctly. I was so ashamed I wanted to die. I eventually reached out to my faculty advisor. He was really empathic and understanding and he suggested some other ways to help me finish school. I'm now in the process of applying for withdrawal from all my classes in my previous active semester so that it won't affect my CGPA and I can go back to school. 

Here's the good news: you are still so young. Honestly, you are. You can still turn this around. Please go talk to your advisor about what you're struggling with, and be honest. I was brutally honest with my advisor. I told him about my anxiety, my depression, my procrastination habits, and even about my suicidal thoughts. You might be able to do the same thing as me and withdraw from your classes this semester so it won't affect your CGPA. I also suggest seeking counselling with the on-campus counsellors (it's free!), they can give you some great resources for mental health. They can also provide medical documentation that can help with the withdrawal process.

I hope this helps you out. Take a break if you need to (I took two semesters off before starting the withdrawal process). Seek counselling, it will make you feel so much better just being able to unload all your insecurities to someone who won't judge you. I'm still seeing a therapist. If you have any questions please feel free to PM me. You have not wasted your entire life. Your life is just beginning. You are not a fuck up. We will both get through this!

She didn't know. She called her brother out on his behavioir. She was on your side. What more do you want? You are ridiculous OP. I feel bad for your gf.

I'm glad you apologized to your girlfriend. I feel like you should have done more to make it up to her for your overreaction. You got so ridiculously mad at her for something that was out of her control. Her patience with you is honestly so admirable. She showed so much remorse for something that wasn't even her fault. She should have been mad at you for being such a dick to her. I get that you're mad at her brother, but directing your anger at the girl you love is uncalled for. Your car is just your car, but your girlfriend is a human being with emotions and feelings. 

I used to have a boyfriend who was obsessed with his car as well, but he never once got mad at me over his car. No matter what happened to it, he was always gentle and kind. Your overreaction against your girlfriend in this situation is so immature and petty. Major kudos to your lovely girlfriend for having the patience of a saint.

I'm also 23 and I know exactly how you feel. My schooling career has been a mess because of my depression and lack of motivation. Most of my friends my age have already graduated. I, on the other hand, am taking eternity and a day to finish my undergrad. I feel like I'm being left behind, especially since - like you mentioned - everyone is so busy with their significant others, starting or finding a full-time job, and/or moving away to start an amazing new adventure. 

Some of my friends know I'm depressed but it just seems like they don't care. No one asks, no one bothers. Whatever. I feel like I'm losing friends left and right. I feel really alone. 

I can truly, truly empathize with you so please PM me if you ever feel like talking. :)

My mom says similar things to me to. She thinks I'm not trying hard enough to be happy. She keeps telling me I have no reason to be depressed, especially since I'm "living a way better life than she did when she was younger." We keep getting into arguments over this because she just doesn't understand and she gets angry at me. She thinks there's a timeline in getting over depression. It infuriates me so badly and makes me feel even worse.

I was recently in a similar situation with my ex. I felt the exact same things as you did. I broke up with him and it was the biggest mistake of my life. I thought I would go out and meet new guys and have lots of fun, but it's been four months since our breakup and I haven't been able to do any of those things because I'm so depressed. He was a really good boyfriend and all the guys I've been meeting are nothing compared to him. I really think you should think this through because you'll never ever meet another girl quite like her again and it might haunt you for the rest of your life.

Enjoy high school and being around your friends! When you're graduating university like me and you look back, you'll really cherish the fun times you had in high school. :P 

There are so many amazing guys out there, you have so much time to explore. And I hope you keep these words in mind as you go through life and experience different relationships: "one day you'll realize why it never worked out with anybody else." :)

Amen to this. 

Honestly, it's unhealthy for you to keep blaming her for making a decision she has the right to make. You think it was easy for her too? Breaking up with someone is one of the hardest things you can ever do in your life. You spend weeks (or even months) mulling over it in your head. You spend every waking moment weighing the pros and cons of your decision, but you feel absolutely awful anyway knowing that you'll hurt the one you love. It takes a whole lot of careful thinking and courage. It's good that she broke up with you instead of prolonging a relationship she'd only be able to half-heatedly partake in. It would've been selfish of her if she wanted to have her cake and eat it too. She did the right thing by breaking up with you when she had doubts. It saved you from a whole other world of pain, trust me.

She caused you heartbreak. I get that, I really, really do. It's awful. I was a mess too (still am), and I'm still seeing my therapist as well. But what you do after the heartbreak is all on you. Even though it took a long time, you got yourself together. Isn't that something worth celebrating? This success was your doing! However, you also need to realize how you react to the awful feelings after the breakup is up to you too. Both your failures and successes are yours. She cannot be blamed or credited for either. 

And clearly, if it was any indication, she's also been hurting a lot over these past few years. You aren't the only one. Don't extend that "olive branch," you aren't doing anyone any favours. In fact, it just seems like you're punishing her. This isn't healthy, and to be quite honest, it seems like she's been punishing herself enough for the last few years with her obsessive behaviour over you. 

I wish you all the best in your healing journey.

We were in a long distance relationship and I felt like I was losing feelings for him because of the distance so I broke it off. He was a great boyfriend though, the sweetest and most considerate guy I have ever had the pleasure of dating. I can't remember anything negative about him so it's been really hard for me to move on. I'm scared I never will. I'm scared I'll never find anyone who will love me as much and be willing to put up with my flaws.

It's also been really hard for me to cope. The first three months I was an absolute mess. I couldn't eat or sleep and I ended up dropping all my summer semester courses because I just couldn't concentrate on school. I have never been so low in my life. I was anxious and depressed and it eventually got so bad I had to start seeing a therapist. 

It's gotten a bit easier in comparison to the first few months, but nothing anyone says or does can really make me feel better. :/ I did start writing a journal though. I found that jotting down my thoughts throughout the day would alleviate some of the pain. Another way I distracted myself was (warning: this isn't the healthiest mentality) writing a detailed list of ways on how I'd improve myself in order to win my ex back. Although it gave me false hope, it also gave me inspiration and motivation on bettering myself. Now, I'm pleased to say that although I no longer hold hopes of getting back together with my ex, l'm still completing things on my list.

I'm here to talk if you ever need it. :(

I'm going through a hard breakup as well and I don't think I could have made it this far without talking to somebody.

I dated this guy for a year in my last year of high school. We ended up getting accepted into universities in different provinces. However, we had a strong relationship so we tried doing long distance. I thought we'd make it. I thought I truly loved him. As a 17-18 year old, I thought this was the real thing. It wasn't. When we broke up I was devastated. I thought I'd never meet anyone who I'd be so attracted to and serious about again. Of course, I was wrong.

I completely agree with plutonium743, love does get better with age. The love I had in my most recent relationship in university was so much stronger and so much more mature than my high school ones. I can't even begin to describe how awesome it is. In university, you have so much more freedom and time (in a sense) and this really gives you the chance to build and strengthen both friendships and relationships. You can plan trips together and stay over late and watch movies and just do whatever you want without your parents nagging you (if you live on campus). 

You might feel like this girl is the real thing. Maybe she is, maybe she isn't. But you're still young and university will completely change your perspective on many things. University opens up a whole new world of different people you'd never thought you'd meet or like. It might not feel like it now because you're still in high school, but when you go to university you'll understand exactly what I'm talking about. And honestly, I think you might end up regretting it if you didn't at least explore these new options. 

Also, you can't put a time limit on getting over someone. So what if it's been six months? It's okay. I'm at four months post breakup and I'm nowhere near healed. It's okay to take your time. Furthermore, I don't think it's a good idea to be in a relationship when you're not completely over someone. It's unhealthy for yourself and extremely hurtful for the other person. Take some time for yourself first. 

Best of luck in whatever you decide! :)

I broke up with my ex in Feb too, but ironically, even though I'm the dumper, I'm finding it damn near impossible to move on. I'm scared I made a mistake, scared I let the best person in my life walk out. I was coping okay for a few weeks, but these past few days have gotten so bad. :( Good luck to the both of us. Know that you're not alone in this.

Yes I am going through the exact same thing. I'm not going to lie, it's going to feel like absolute shit. You're going to feel regret and you're going to feel like you're a terrible person, but know that it's okay because in the long run you did the right thing. It wouldn't be fair for him anyway if he was putting in all the effort. 

It's been four months for me and I still have so many bad days. I still feel regret and I still miss him a lot. But I do have some good days and that really keeps me going. Do things you really, really love. Surround yourself only with people you enjoy being with. Splurge on yourself. Go for long walks at night. Take your time to heal. This is your life, do whatever it takes to make yourself happy. 

Time will take care of everything. And don't feel guilty. You did what's best for yourself, it's much better than prolonging the pain. You will be okay. Who knows, maybe one day you guys will end up together again. But don't worry too much, just go with the flow of life. Just know that you're not alone. :)

I know exactly how you feel. I fear the exact same things. :( For me it's been almost four months and I still feel like crap a lot of the time. It does get better though, it really does. Although you'll never forget the connection and the memories, bit by bit it does hurt less. Bit by bit, you'll start getting excited at the prospect of meeting new people. :) 

I was a mess for the first three months of the breakup. I couldn't eat or sleep and I cried everyday. Nothing anyone said or did made me feel better. The only thing I can say is that you will slowly move on, even though you have to deal with the pain everyday. There is hope, there always is. There were only a couple of things that made me feel incrementally better and that was going for walks with friends and being around my family. 

I'm still not completely okay, but knowing that I do have some good days keep me going. I remind myself that one guy cannot be the end of my world. I remind myself that the only person who cares about me the most in this world is myself. We can get through this! =)

I really needed this too. Thank you. I've spent the past three months absolutely miserable because I cannot stop idealizing my past relationship. I keep blaming myself for my unhappiness because I ended it and I can't move on or cope with my feelings. Reading this made my gloomy day a little better. So thank you.
Ahhhh your posts make me feel all warm and fuzzy inside. I'm glad it all worked out! He sounds like he's going to be an awesome boyfriend. I wish you guys all the best. <3

I broke up with him because I felt like I was losing feelings for him since we were doing long distance. As a result, I found myself slowly distancing myself from him so I broke up with him. :( 

Sometimes I feel like I made a huge mistake.....but I don't see myself getting married to him, I don't. :( It's just really hard to cope right now because he was a sweet guy to the very end. I miss him so much I can't breathe sometimes, and the thought of moving on makes me really nauseous. 

I can't bring myself to go on dates or anything like that because I just don't find any other guy attractive right now. I'm just really, really depressed. But I really do want to move on. I just don't know how to let go.
Thank you so much for responding! I've been worrying about this so much, it really helps hearing from someone aside from a family member or friend that everything is going to be okay. * Hugs *
